title: Tu Youyou (1930–) — Project 523, Artemisinin, the 2011 Lasker & China's First Science Nobel

teenKit.tldr: In the middle of political chaos, researcher Tu Youyou stared down 190 failed experiments to find a life-saving malaria cure hidden in a 1,600-year-old medical text. By reading ancient words literally instead of poetically, she unlocked artemisinin and saved millions of lives.
teenKit.whyItMatters: This breakthrough proves that world-changing innovations often hide in plain sight if you have the discipline to look past old traditions and follow the exact data.
keyTakeaways: Tu Youyou refused to give up after 190 failed chemical extractions, turning failure into a strict roadmap for success.
She realized that boiling herbs destroyed the active medicine, changing her extraction method because she read an ancient text literally.
By combining modern laboratory science with historical primary texts, she solved a global health crisis that stumped top researchers for decades.

quiz.question: Why did Tu Youyou's initial 190 experiments with the sweet wormwood plant fail?
options: She was using the wrong plant species entirely.
She was following the traditional method of boiling the herbs into a hot soup, which destroyed the heat-sensitive medicine.
The mice she tested them on had a genetic immunity to malaria.
The laboratory equipment was too modern and contaminated the samples.
quiz.explanation: Boiling the plant destroyed its healing compounds, whereas soaking it cold (as the ancient text literally suggested) preserved them.

quiz.question: What made Tu Youyou's interpretation of the 1,600-year-old Taoist text different from everyone else who read it before her?
options: She read it as a strict chemical blueprint rather than dismissing it as poetic folklore.
She was the only person in China who could read ancient Chinese characters.
She altered the text to fit her own preconceived theories.
She translated it into English for the first time.
quiz.explanation: While others saw the text as a quaint ancient recipe, she treated its instructions for cold-water extraction as a precise experimental variable.

quiz.question: What major global recognition did Tu Youyou eventually receive for her discovery of artemisinin?
options: An Academy Award for documentary filmmaking
The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
quiz.explanation: Her groundbreaking isolation of artemisinin earned her China's first science Nobel Prize in 2015.
